newsitem.title: USA: Early returns show U.S. brokerages had solid Q1.
newsitem.headline: Early returns show U.S. brokerages had solid Q1.

text.p: Initial earnings reports from Wall Street brokerages show the industry enjoyed a solidly profitable first quarter despite a sizable stock market decline at the end of March.
Investor response to the earnings reports was muted, however, as many looked past the current quarter and focused on the industry's uncertain outlook.
"The quarter looks very strong," said Sallie Krawcheck, an analyst at Sanford C. Bernstein. "The problem is the quarter mostly represents the period before the market turned (down)."
Early Monday, Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette reported stronger-than-expected first quarter earnings. Travelers Group Inc also topped estimates, helped by record earnings at its Smith Barney unit.

Travelers posted operating earnings of $0.95 per share, up from $0.71 a year ago and ahead of First Call's $0.91 consensus estimate. DLJ earned $1.35 per share, up from $1.01 a year ago and well ahead of a $1.06 First Call estimate.

Jefferies Group Inc, a smaller firm that handles institutional trading and offers advisory services to small and mid-sized companies also posted strong numbers, with earnings rising to $1.01 per share from $0.88 last year. No First Call estimate was available.
But the reality of a declining market was evident in Travelers' comment that Smith Barney's performance in March "was not as robust as the quarter's first months."
Analysts were not surprised, noting some underlying trends that have investment firms under pressure.
"Underwriting is really drying up," Krawcheck said, a factor that was noticeable in Smith Barney's five percent decline in investment banking revenues versus a year ago.
Even amid signs of a less-friendly market environment, Jefferies chief executive Frank Baxter said he believed his firm was well-positioned to build on the quarter.

"Our compensation is quite variable, so when revenues go down, costs also go down," he said. He also said the small- and mid-cap clients that Jefferies advises in an investment banking capacity "are growing and still need financing."
Even so, he acknowledged, "the preferred market environment would be up and this seven-year bull market is looking a little long in the tooth."
Shares in DLJ dipped 3/8 to 37-1/2 and Jefferies Group shed 1/8 to 43-1/8. Travelers Group rallied in early afternoon trade, rising 1-1/4 to 47-5/8.
